title: Cross-Cloud Identity Correlation

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `OR index=azure OR index=gcp` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.4.2 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `OR index=azure OR index=gcp`. Confirm UC-4.4.2 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via Combined cloud TAs + lookup tables; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" OR index=azure OR index=gcp
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.2_cross_cloud_identity_cor_2"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.4.2 — Cross-Cloud Identity Correlation: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:cloudtrail` for search criteria `OR index=azure OR index=gcp` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), detecting 'Cross-Cloud Identity Correlation' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.2 drives medium-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Create a lookup table mapping cloud identities to a normalized user (e.g., email). Combine audit logs from all three providers. Dashboard showing cross-cloud activity per user.
visualization: Table (user, clouds, activity count), Sankey diagram (user to cloud to action).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Combined cloud TAs + lookup tables with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Create a lookup table mapping cloud identities to a normalized user (e.g., email). Combine audit logs from all three providers. Dashboard showing cross-cloud activity per user.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" OR index=azure OR index=gcp
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.2_cross_cloud_identity_cor_2"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect cross-cloud identity correlation. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_2_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (user, clouds, activity count), Sankey diagram (user to cloud to action)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Combined cloud TAs + lookup tables and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cross-cloud identity correlation so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
